c0: Today, the Reserve Bank released the results of the December 2018 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH) 1 2 . The survey was conducted in 18 cities and the results are based on responses from 5,828 urban households. Highlights: i. The proportion of respondents expecting general prices to rise in the next three months and one year ahead horizons fell sharply in relation to the November 2018 round with a similar pattern observed in respect of most of the product groups, and especially for food and non-food products ( Table 1a and 1b ). ii. Respondents also moderated their expectations with respect to the rate of future price changes. ( Table 1a and 1b ). iii. In quantitative terms, three months ahead and one year ahead median inflation expectations dropped by 80 and 130 basis points (bps), respectively, from their readings in the November 2018 round ( Chart 1 , Table 2 ). iv. The decline in quantitative expectations was observed across various groups of the respondents ( Table 2 ). Note: Please see the excel file for time series data .
